newsitem.title: USA: Metromedia says shareholders okay sale.
newsitem.headline: Metromedia says shareholders okay sale.

text.p: Metromedia International Group Inc Thursday said its stockholders approved the sale of its entertainment assets to P&F Acquisition Corp, parent of film studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc, for $573 million.
In a statement, Metromedia said funds from the sale will be used to reduce debt and provide capital for expansion of its international communications businesses.
The Metromedia assets include a film and television library with roughly 2,200 titles and movie production companies, Orion Pictures Corp, Motion Picture Corp of America and Goldwyn Entertainment Co.
Metromedia will keep the Landmark Theatre Group, with 139 movie screens at 49 theaters in the United States.
MGM studios are co-owned by billionaire Kirk Kerkorian's investment company, Tracinda Corp, and Australian media conglomerate Seven Network Ltd.
